- When sentiment is negative and forecast is trending upward, reduce forecast by 5–10% to avoid overcorrection.  
- If recent price spike is followed by model overshoot, apply a 1–2 day lag correction to smooth out the peak.  
- When sentiment is positive and forecast is trending downward, adjust upward by 3–5% to avoid missing bullish momentum.  
- If 30-day forecast mean is significantly below recent 18-day average, assume mean reversion and raise forecast slightly.  
- If sentiment is consistently negative over 5+ days, suppress forecast volatility and favor conservative, downward-trending path.  
- If forecast shows sharp upward movement after a dip, check sentiment for bullish reversal — if sentiment is weak, cap upward momentum at 1–2% above prior peak.
